transcript.text: Hi, I've got a Dyson V15 Detect (SV22) about 4 months old. When I go from the kitchen tiles onto the lounge rug the motor suddenly gets much louder and the battery number drops faster, then it calms down again when I go back on the tiles. Also the screen goes up and down by itself. Is the motor on its way out? It's still under guarantee so I want to report it before it dies completely.

From what you describe, the motor almost probably isn't failing. This sounds like the vacuum doing what it's designed to do. V15 Detect machines typically have an Auto mode. When it goes onto a rug or carpet it automatically turns the suction up, so the motor gets noticeably louder. When it goes back onto hard floor it drops the power again. The number on the screen is an estimate of the remaining run time, not a fixed countdown. It recalculates as the power changes. So it falls faster on the rug and can creep back up on the tiles. That matches what you're seeing. A motor that is genuinely wearing out sounds different. It's usually a rough grinding, screeching or high whine all the time, or the machine pulses, cuts out or smells hot. It wouldn't settle neatly back down on tiles. 1. Look at the mode shown on the screen. If it says Auto, switch to Eco or Medium (normally the mode button) and go back onto the rug. If the sound and power now stay steady on both floors, it's Auto mode working and nothing is wrong.
2. With it switched off and the battery not charging, empty the bin. Wash the filter in cold water and let it dry fully (at least 24 hours). A clogged filter makes the motor labour harder, especially on carpet. If it was dirty and the strain eases afterwards, that was adding to it.
3. Turn the floorhead over and clear any hair or thread from the brush bar. Check it turns freely by hand. A tangled bar drags more on a rug, and the machine responds by working harder. If it still roars or strains on the rug even in Eco or Medium, contact Dyson under the guarantee. The same applies if you ever hear grinding or screeching, it pulses or cuts out, or it shows an error on the screen. At 4 months old it's fully covered, so it's worth reporting if it does turn out to be a fault.

Thank you, I've tried those. The screen says 'Auto', and when I switched to Eco the sound stays the same quiet level on both the rug and the tiles. I washed the filter last month and let it dry for a day, and the brush bar is clean with no hair on it. There's no burning smell, no heat and no warning lights. So is Auto mode simply meant to do this, and is there nothing wrong with the motor?

Yes, that's Auto mode doing its job, and nothing you've described points to a motor problem. Your Eco test is the clincher. In Eco the power is fixed, and it stayed at the same quiet level on both the rug and the tiles. So the motor itself is steady. The extra noise in Auto is simply the machine choosing to turn the power up when it senses carpet. A failing motor wouldn't behave neatly like that. It would sound rough, grind, screech or whine all the time, whatever the mode or floor. The screen behaves the same way. In Auto the runtime figure keeps recalculating as the power level changes. It dropping on the rug and recovering on the tiles is expected. There's nothing to report under the guarantee at the moment. If you'd like a quieter clean with longer battery life, use Eco or Medium for routine jobs and keep Auto for when you want the extra pull on rugs. Keep washing the filter about once a month as you have been, and always let it dry fully. It would be worth contacting Dyson while it's covered if you notice any of these:
1. Grinding, screeching or a rattling noise.
2. Pulsing on and off, or cutting out.
3. A burning smell, or the body getting hot.
4. An error or warning on the screen.
5. The runtime getting much shorter on Eco than when it was new. None of those apply now, so you can carry on using it with confidence.
